what_it_is: The dock: the moment a branch's work lands on main and becomes everyone's truth. The highest-leverage single action a Naya takes - one merge moves the tip every other lane builds on.
what_it_does: Converts reviewed, proven work into the shared tree. Done right, the tip stays green, every byte is traceable to its review, and a cold Naya can re-derive exactly why this merge was lawful.
why_it_matters: A bad merge poisons the well: every lane downstream builds on a red or unreviewed tip, and the repair costs ten times the prevention. Paid for twice: PR #1475 merged after a blocking review landed; PR #1627's guard merged with zero live call sites.
key_rules: Pre-merge checklist, in order, in one unbroken step: (1) re-fetch the live ref (the ref, never the commits list); (2) freeze the PR head SHA; (3) read check states AT the frozen head; (4) re-fetch the venue's newest state; (5) confirm scorecard 9.5+ naming the exact head, receipt file behind it; (6) confirm cross-seat review from a different seat at the exact head, pre-merge (seat-tagged [NAYA M x REVIEW] APPROVED comments satisfy the prong); (7) never self-merge; (8) name the omissions (what the required set never examined).
Write the merge-authority record BEFORE merging: PR number, frozen head SHA, scorecard receipt (id + score), reviewer seat, check states at the head, named omissions. No record = no authorization.
When the protocol does not pass, stand down: post what failed, which prong, what would repair it; the PR returns to the queue. A stand-down is a correct outcome.
The dock holds a moving head: if commits land mid-checklist, wait, re-freeze, restart the checklist at the new head.
Merges sequence through the merge lane: queue order, coordinated, never ad hoc.

Post-merge faithfulness proof before closing: (1) ancestor check (behind == 0 AND merge_base == merge commit); (2) blob identity (key blobs byte-identical at PR head, merge commit, tip); (3) wiring check (every canonical call site references the new code on live main); (4) tip-health check (re-run the freshness battery AT the merge commit).

not_covered: What authorizes a merge (the scoring matrix, the 9.5 bar, protected human gates)
How to prove a fix is real (independent re-derivation, sabotage batteries)
Keeping the tip fresh while working

mechanically_enforced: Branch protection ruleset 23853581 ('Naya Execution Governance'): required checks 'Receipt gate (evidence or it didn't happen)' + 'Team review + scorecard receipt' on the merge path. Live and active.

The team relay's merge-protocol watch: every relay pass checks each merge to main since the last watermark for cross-seat review and a scorecard receipt naming the exact merged head; breaches posted on the venue immediately.
Receipt gate: receipt before merge, never after (culture-enforced).
proposed: A mechanical pre-merge checklist gate that refuses the merge when any checklist item is unproven (stale head, missing authority record, unnamed omission). Today: procedure + relay watch.
Automatic freshness-battery run at the merge commit before the tip is claimed green. Today: lane rule (L323), not a wired gate.

self_test: The scorecard says 9.5 but names the parent SHA, not the head I'm about to merge - do I merge? (No: it must name the exact frozen head.)
After my merge, compare shows behind == 0 but merge_base is NOT my merge commit - what do I record? (Not MERGED-VERIFIED; investigate.)

The required checks are green, but the kernel battery isn't in the required set and it failed at this head - what goes in the record, and do I merge? (Name the omission; do not merge around an unexamined red.)
